headline: US bitcoin funds are net sellers for 2026 after their worst week since June, as Binance swaps its finance chief and keeps cleaning up after its record hack.

stories.title: US bitcoin funds turn negative for 2026 after a $1.28B outflow week
stories.summary: Investors pulled a net $1.28 billion from US spot bitcoin ETFs in the week of 2-6 November, the worst week since late June. That wiped out the year's inflows: the funds are now net sellers for 2026. Bitcoin dropped to an 11-week low on Friday after a strong US jobs report raised bets on a Fed rate hike.
points: Net flows by day: Mon -$398.6M, Tue -$115.6M, Wed +$74.6M, Thu -$430.2M, Fri -$411.9M, per The Block.
The funds are now about -$914.1M for 2026, after starting the week about +$368M, per The Block.
Ether ETFs lost $365.3M, their sixth negative week in a row, per The Block.
Bitcoin fell to $74,762 on Friday, its lowest since 21 August, after US jobs came in at 165K versus 65K expected, per Cointelegraph.
CME FedWatch odds of a December rate hike rose from 66.9% to 76.8% after the jobs report, per Cointelegraph.

sources.label: The Block: bitcoin ETFs flip negative for 2026

stories.title: Binance changes finance chief as hack clean-up continues
stories.summary: Binance co-CEO Yi He said CFO Kaiser Ng is leaving, with Justin Yek taking over, and that the handover was planned six months ago, before the hack. Blockchain analysts say billions of the stolen funds have not yet been laundered, and six tokens are due to reopen for withdrawals before next weekend.
points: Yek was previously VP of finance at Airwallex, per The Block.
The hack's size differs by source: $6.43B per Elliptic via Decrypt, $6.3B per Cointelegraph.
About $3.11B still sits in hacker-linked addresses, about $2.85B has been frozen or seized, and about $124M has been swapped into bitcoin, per Elliptic via Decrypt.
Investigators say North Korea-linked hackers took over an employee's device about eight weeks before the attack using a fake recruitment scheme, per the Security Alliance via Cointelegraph.
Binance plans to reopen withdrawals for HYPE, INJ, APT, PLASMA, NEAR and LTC before the 14-15 Nov weekend, per TokenPost.

stories.title: US Treasury moves to cut exchange MEXC off from the US financial system
stories.summary: The Treasury's financial-crimes unit, FinCEN, ordered US financial institutions to stop processing transfers involving MEXC Global, alleging billions in illicit flows tied to Iran, North Korea and Russia. MEXC says it is operating normally and reviewing the order.
points: FinCEN alleges at least $16B of illicit flows over five years, per CoinDesk.
That includes about $1.5B linked to Russian sanctions evasion and about $1B sent to more than 40 Iranian exchanges, per CoinDesk.
The order takes effect 30 days after it is published in the Federal Register, per CoinDesk.
MEXC says it has started an independent review of its anti-money-laundering controls, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Binance closing accounts in some EU countries
briefs.summary: Users in Spain, France, Poland and Italy were told to withdraw; a monthly fee of 0.025% of the balance starts 29 Nov and accounts close 31 Dec, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Gnosis Pay data breach
briefs.summary: The crypto debit-card provider says card numbers, home addresses and linked wallet addresses were exposed; it says funds were not affected. Watch for phishing messages, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Korean exchange GOPAX pauses after a hack threat
briefs.summary: GOPAX suspended trading and standard withdrawals after an emailed threat and is moving assets to offline storage; it says nothing has been stolen, per Cointelegraph.

briefs.title: Crypto-in-401(k) rule under White House review
briefs.summary: The Labor Department's proposal names no specific coins, and the review can take up to 90 days, per Cointelegraph.

briefs.title: Treasury walks back its travel-rule plan
briefs.summary: The US Treasury withdrew a proposal to tighten recordkeeping on crypto transfers, per The Block.

briefs.title: Ex-FBI agent pleads guilty to crypto theft
briefs.summary: He admitted stealing $2.47M in crypto from wallets tied to 35 investigations, per The Block.

briefs.title: Strive adds 15,124 BTC in October
briefs.summary: The purchase moves Strive closer to the largest corporate bitcoin holders, per Cointelegraph.
